end.summary:
Named energy sources including food, sunlight, wind, flowing water, fuels and electricity.
Matched examples: food–running, wind–kite, electricity–fan, petrol–car and gas–stove.
Explained the wind-to-electricity chain: blades, generator and wires to a TV.
Initially questioned whether wind has energy; later stated that moving air turns blades and produces electricity.
Teach-back was not yet completed.
end.parentNote: Prisha practised matching energy sources with what they make work and used examples such as a kite, fan, car and stove. They connected moving air to blades, a generator and wires carrying electricity to a TV. The mix-up about wind having energy was corrected later in the lesson, although the full teach-back was not completed. At home, ask them to sort everyday examples into source and use, such as sunlight–solar panel and flowing water–water wheel.
